### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **28** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-packaged-base-refusal.ts`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/served-override.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**22** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 69244406b7e93b8856f3a5991ec18433a7e96dc4`.

⛔ **6** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-packaged-base-refusal.ts`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/served-override.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **64** of **227** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **181** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 69244406b7e93b8856f3a5991ec18433a7e96dc4` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d78082473b688919a7ac5f714d8a32281912235e` — the merge of head `e73f5c2c17c08a844a987bb42ce55bf780f4b3e7` into base `69244406b7e93b8856f3a5991ec18433a7e96dc4`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d78082473b688919a7ac5f714d8a32281912235e && git checkout d78082473b688919a7ac5f714d8a32281912235e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 69244406b7e93b8856f3a5991ec18433a7e96dc4 e73f5c2c17c08a844a987bb42ce55bf780f4b3e7 && git checkout -B drift-repro 69244406b7e93b8856f3a5991ec18433a7e96dc4 && git merge --no-ff e73f5c2c17c08a844a987bb42ce55bf780f4b3e7

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 69244406b7e93b8856f3a5991ec18433a7e96dc4
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 69244406b7e93b8856f3a5991ec18433a7e96dc4` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a4cbe87c92decad6eaa7ca3daa58845077d685b7`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/kernel/override-declaration.zod.ts + packages/objectql/src/package-upgrade-environment.ts, packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/served-override.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-packaged-base-refusal.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/package/install.ts

Inputs read: card #30886 (body and all six comments, the scope addition 6683318926 and the os-dev-report 6724770924 included), PR #31627 body, file list and the net diff against `main` (merge-base `95df3459`, 31 files, +537/-63), the check-runs on the head, and the cited code in the live tree (ADR-0146 D2 as amended, `protocol-served-overrides.ts`, `stack-collections.ts`, `artifact-packages.ts`, `engine-top-level.ts`, `engine-registration.ts`, `registry.ts`, `item-key-discriminators.ts`, `canonicalize.ts`, `manifest-collection-spelling.ts`, `customization-package.ts`, `view.zod.ts`, `marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts`, `kernel.ts`). The rest of the diff (tests, the 18 regenerated reference pages, the two hand-written docs pages, the changeset) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set: unchanged — right.** No door refuses more or less. The install-local schema refusal reads `environment.columns` only (`readSchemaUpgradeRows`, `marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts`), the finding-set token is computed from the schema plan, and the dry run forwards `environment` whole (`answerUpgradeDryRun`). `marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts` is not in the diff. The ADR's sentence "an advisory class that its refusal never reads and that no finding-set token covers" holds in the tree, not only in the PR body.
- **Public surface: `manifest.planUpgrade` response gains `environment.overrides` (`{ hidesChange, stale } | null`) — right, additive.** `PackageUpgradeEnvironment` gains a required `overrides` member, but the type is package-internal: `packages/objectql/src/index.ts` exports nothing from `package-upgrade-environment.ts` (only `ObjectQLPlugin` from `plugin.ts`), so no published TypeScript surface moves. No `packages/spec` zod carries the plan's shape — the claim amendment 6723756312 reading is confirmed, the spec red line does not apply.
- **CLI surface: `os package install --dry-run` prints two advisory sections and a `null` line — right.** `renderUpgradePlan` reads `env.overrides` only when present; a runtime that predates the key prints nothing new.
- **Spec surface: `.describe()` / JSDoc text only — right.** `OverrideDeclarationSchema.shape.basedOn` stays `z.string().min(1)`; no key, value or requirement moves, so `Metadata-protocol: none` is the correct declaration. The 18 `content/docs/references/**` pages are the generator's output of that text (`check:docs`); the head's `Lint & Repo Gates` is green.
- **Metadata-protocol surface: comments only — right.** `isServedOverrideRowOf` and `refusePackagedBaseOverride` are byte-identical in logic; neither reads `overrides.basedOn` (the refusal file reads the BASE's `manifest.version` to prescribe a declaration, lines 503–507, which is not a read of a declaration's `basedOn`).

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/30886-upgrade-plan-override-advisories.md`: `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/spec` at `patch`, both declaration lines at line start (`Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`), the same two lines line-initial in the PR body. The level follows the kind alone (Post-Task Checklist 3): kind `none` takes `patch`, so `patch` on all three is right even though the title is `feat(…)`; the widening is non-breaking, so no BREAKING banner and no ADR-0087 disposition is owed. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is the right arm: a new response key, nothing refused that was accepted. `Check Changeset` on the head: success.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev `open_questions` (report 6724770924), each answered here:

1. **An override whose stored body records no `basedOn` is not listed as stale — A, accepted.** The declaration schema requires `basedOn` (`min(1)`), `listServedOverrides` emits `basedOn` only when the stored body carries a string, and a finding with no version to date would prescribe nothing. The hides-change finding still lists such a row, so it is not invisible.
2. **`hidesChange` also lists `removed` and `added` base items — A, accepted.** ADR-0146 D2 as amended charters finding (a) for "a base item the upgrade changes between the installed and the new version"; an item the new version drops or newly ships under an overridden name is a change the override now shadows, the `change` discriminator keeps the three apart, and nothing is refused on any of them. Advisory, inside the amendment's wording.
3. **Field name `environment.overrides` — A, accepted.** It rides every reader that forwards `environment` whole (the dry run, cloud's 01c preview) and the refusal reads `environment.columns` only; a new top-level key would have needed a door change for no gain.

Dev `deviations`: `plugin.ts` edited under claim amendment 6723756312 (the `planUpgrade` closure only — confirmed, the diff touches lines 79 and 1042–1060 only); `override-declaration.test.ts` edited as a forced pin of the wording the card itself orders changed — declared, accepted; ablation A2 first run vacuous then fixed — declared, accepted; PR assignee not set — a relay matter, not this review's; `test:repo` not run locally — CI `Test Core` runs it (in progress at reading time). The dev's out-of-scope note (`protocol-served-overrides.ts:45-47` and `package-lifecycle.zod.ts:536` describe the customizations read, which still judges nothing) is read and agreed: those sentences stay true and are not edited. Governed quotes (`docs/adr/0126-…:3`, `skills/objectstack-platform/evals/config-plugins-ops.json:169`) are not touched — confirmed on the file list. Nothing to escalate.

Check-runs on the head at reading time: success — `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `Spec property liveness`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Build Docs`, `Build UI Deps`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `PR-body guards`, `Check Documentation Links`, all `Lint ·` lanes; in progress — `Test Core (1–8/8)`, `Build Core`, `Type Check · workspace / consumer gates / debt ledger`, `Type Check UI`, `Test UI (1–16/16)`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Live E2E UI`; skipped — the opt-in harnesses. No failure recorded. The landing still waits for the required set to go green.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/kernel/override-declaration.zod.ts` (hits) against ADR-0146 D2 as amended and its first consumer.** The `basedOn` description now says: recorded, never a gate; nothing refused, merged or rebased on it; one reader, as advice — a base's upgrade plan lists an override whose `basedOn` is not the installed base version as stale, beside each override whose base item the upgrade changes. That is D2's amended paragraph sentence by sentence: finding (a) hides-change, finding (b) stale, "no door refuses, no token is asked, and nothing is merged, rebased or rewritten automatically", and the Consequences bullet "the upgrade plan's advisory finding … refuses, merges and rebases nothing". The `overrides` JSDoc and `.describe()` say the same in short form. The first consumer, `readOverrideAdvisories`, does exactly what the text says and nothing more: `stale` is `basedOn !== installedVersion`, `hidesChange` is a body comparison, both pushed into an advisory class nobody refuses on. The old sentence "no upgrade diff is produced from it" is gone, which the scope addition 6683318926 required. The pin in `override-declaration.test.ts` reads the new wording. No finding.

**`packages/metadata-protocol/src/served-override.ts` and `protocol-packaged-base-refusal.ts` (implementing files, comment-only hunks).** Both sentences describe code that does not read `overrides.basedOn` — verified: `isServedOverrideRowOf` reads `package_id`, `type` and `overrides.package`; the refusal file's `basedOn` occurrences are the prescription it writes from the base's `manifest.version`. "Its one reader is a base's upgrade plan, as advice" is the ADR's own vocabulary ("One reader is admitted, as advice"); the customizations read copies the value without judging it, which is not a reader in that sense. No finding.

**`packages/objectql/src/package-upgrade-environment.ts` (implementing file).** Read against the contract and the code it cites:

- Package bodies: `stackPackageBodies` unwraps `packages[].manifest` (`resolveArtifactPackageOrder` → `entry.manifest`), the one-package shape falls back to the artifact itself; the install door flattens a nested single-manifest bundle before `planUpgrade` (`normalizeBundle` → `flattenPackageBody`) and the ledger stores that flattened body, so `body.id` and `body.version` are at the top level on both sides. The dev's `ObjectQLPlugin` test exercises the multi-package shape through the real service. Right.
- Item identity: `METADATA_ARRAY_KEYS` + `resolveMetadataItemName` is the engine's own collection seam (`registerMetadataCollections`), `pluralToSingular` folds every key in that list to the type the stored row carries (`views → view`, `emailTemplates → email_template`, …), `itemDiscriminator` is the one identity table (`email_template` by `locale`, canonical `en-US`) and `listServedOverrides` keys its answer the same way (type, name, `bundle_member`). A view container is enumerated under its object and as the items `expandViewContainer` makes, which is how Studio names the override row (`acme_lead.all`). Right.
- Comparison: `canonicalize` (sorted-key stable JSON) over the body with the loader's `_`-prefixed stamps removed, so `_packageVersion` does not make every item differ. Right, and ablated (A1, A2).
- Failure shape: `null` when no reader is given or any read throws, told once through `warn`, never `[]` — the module's existing "never taken for zero" rule, and the read-seam invention rule's intent. Right.
- Advisory class: pushed into `environment.overrides` alone; `plan` is untouched; the door's refusal and token never see it (A5). Right.

**Should-fix — the `app` type is overridable and is never enumerated, so an overridden app can never earn a hides-change finding.** `OVERRIDE_TYPE_CLASSIFICATION` (`customization-package.ts`) lists `app` as overridable. The engine registers a package's apps outside `METADATA_ARRAY_KEYS`: `apps[]` entries through `registerApp` (`registry.ts`: `registerItem('app', app, 'name', packageId)`), and the package body itself as an app when it carries `navigation` and no `apps[]` (`engine-registration.ts` line 111, `selfAsApp`). `packageItemTexts` walks `METADATA_ARRAY_KEYS` and the `viewItems` channel only, so for an `app` override `was` and `will` are both `undefined` and `change` is `undefined`: the base's navigation can change between versions under a customer's app override and the plan says nothing — the exact silence the card exists to end, for the item most likely to be overridden by an administrator. The `stale` finding still fires for it, and nothing is refused, so this is not a must-fix; it is a gap in finding (a) for one listed type, with the header sentence "every item one package body ships, by the identity the registry keys it by" overstating what is enumerated. Fix: enumerate `body.apps[]` by `name ?? id` as type `app`, and the body itself as `app` named `body.name` under the same `selfAsApp` condition the engine uses, by import or by the same predicate — not a third spelling. (`translation` is also listed overridable, but the objectql engine registers no `translation` item from a package body at all, so that type is outside this seam rather than missed by it; a one-line note in the header would make the boundary explicit — nit.)

**Nits (no effect on correctness or the contract):**
- `packageBodiesById` skips a body with no top-level `id` silently; the schema comparison reads collections off the same bodies, so an entry in the nested `packages[i].manifest.manifest` shape is invisible to both halves alike — parity, not a regression.
- `stale` is not listed when the installed body declares no `version` (`installedVersion === null`); there is nothing to compare, and the hides-change finding is unaffected.
- `readOverrideAdvisories` discards advisories already computed for earlier packages when a later package's read throws and answers `null` for the whole class; conservative and consistent with "never a partial answer for a reading that did not happen".

**`packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts` (implementing file).** The closure resolves `protocol` when the plan is asked: `ctx.getService` is the kernel's synchronous lookup and throws on a name nobody registered (`kernel.ts`), the `try/catch` answers `undefined`, and `listOverrides` is passed only when `listServedOverrides` is a function, so a runtime without the protocol answers the class `null`, as the header says. The protocol service is registered under `'protocol'` by `MetadataProtocolPlugin` and by the engine's own `assembleMetadataProtocol` mount, and `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation.listServedOverrides` is the class method the closure calls with `this` bound (`.call(protocol, …)`). One predicate, no re-derivation. No finding.

**`packages/cli/src/commands/package/install.ts` (implementing file).** Prints the two lists after the schema plan, each line ending in the finding's `next`, says so when the class is `null`, prints nothing on a runtime that predates the key. Matches the changeset's "prints both lists after the schema plan". No finding.

Findings: 1 should-fix (`app` items not enumerated for the hides-change finding), 4 nits. No must-fix. The should-fix earns a delta review of its fix on this card; it does not block the landing of this head.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e73f5c2c17c08a844a987bb42ce55bf780f4b3e7`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/kernel/override-declaration.zod.ts + packages/objectql/src/package-upgrade-environment.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-top-level.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-registration.ts, packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/served-override.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-packaged-base-refusal.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/package/install.ts

Delta review of patch round 1, after record 6724918203 on `a4cbe87c92`. Three commits since that head: `f1376fdc` (the fix, 5 files, +58/-7), `a5afea73` (merge of `origin/main` `69244406`), `e73f5c2c` (one regenerated reference page). Read: the fix diff, the merge's effect on the branch (`f1376fdc..a5afea73` on the advisory's seams), the merge's effect against `main` (`a5afea73^2..a5afea73`, which is the PR's own 15 files and nothing else — the merge resolved nothing by hand), the regen commit, claim amendment 6725546518, the changeset at the head, and the check-runs on the head. Everything from the first record that this delta does not name stands as judged there.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set: still unchanged — right.** The fix touches no door. The merge brought `marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts` hunks at the unmanaged-copy region (lines 4869 and 5892) and `protocol.ts` at line 11154 plus imports; none names `planUpgrade`, `answerUpgradeDryRun`, `readSchemaUpgradeRows`, `listServedOverrides`, `convertPackageBodyForward` or `environment` (grep over the merge's added and removed lines on those files: no match). The refusal still reads `environment.columns` only.
- **Public surface of `@objectstack/objectql`: one new export from `engine-top-level.ts`, `registersManifestAsApp` — right, and internal.** `packages/objectql/src/index.ts` does not re-export `engine-top-level.ts`'s free functions; the predicate is consumed by `engine-registration.ts` and `package-upgrade-environment.ts` only. No published surface moves.
- **`@objectstack/metadata-protocol` added to the changeset at `patch` — right.** The PR's hunk in `protocol-packaged-base-refusal.ts` is the JSDoc of `judgeOverrideWrite`, exported from the package index (line 42), so the text ships in `dist/index.d.ts`; a publishing change owes a changeset, and a comment-only change owes nothing above `patch`. `Metadata-protocol: none` stays right in both the PR body and the changeset: nothing an author can write moved.
- **Regenerated `content/docs/references/api/automation-api.mdx` — generated output, the lane seat's.** `Lint & Repo Gates` (which carries `check:docs`) is green on the head, so the committed page is the generator's.

### ② Semver level

Changeset now `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, all `patch`; declaration lines unchanged and line-initial in both places (`Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`). The level follows the kind alone: kind `none` takes `patch`. The added package is the one the first record's ① named as comment-only; naming it is the correct completion, not a level change. `Check Changeset`: success on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Claim amendment 6725546518 adds `engine-top-level.ts` and `engine-registration.ts` to the surface — the diff touches exactly those two files beyond the ones already claimed (plus the changeset and the dev's own test), so the surface and the diff agree.
- The dev's four claims, each verified against the tree rather than taken: (1) `apps[]` and body-as-app enumerated through one exported predicate — verified below; (2) body-as-app compared without `version` — verified (`const { version: _version, ...asApp } = body`); (3) changeset gains metadata-protocol patch — verified; (4) the merge was followed by a regeneration of one page — verified, that commit touches only `content/docs/references/api/automation-api.mdx` (+2/-1).
- No new `open_questions`; the first record's answers stand.
- Check-runs on `e73f5c2c` at reading time: every required context completed with `success` — `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check` (and all four `Type Check ·` lanes), `Test Core` (and 1–8/8), `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Lint UI` (skipped, path-filtered), `Type Check UI`, `Test UI` (and 1–16/16), `Build & E2E UI`, `Live E2E UI`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`; `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `Spec property liveness`, `Build Docs`, `PR-body guards`, `Check Documentation Links` success; the opt-in harnesses skipped. No failure, nothing in progress.

### ④ Design judgment

**Does the fix close the should-fix? Yes.** `packageItemTexts` now (a) walks `body.apps[]` and files each bag under type `app` by `name || id` — the same two-field name the engine's own owner-stamp refusal uses for that loop (`packageBodyObjectAndAppOwnerStampRefusal`: `app?.name || app?.id`); and (b) files the body itself as `app` named `body.name` exactly when `registersManifestAsApp(body)` holds — the predicate `registerApp` step 4 now asks before `registerAppNotingStamp(this._registry, resolved, id, version)`. So the two app shapes the registry serves under type `app` are both enumerated, keyed as `listServedOverrides` keys an `app` row (type, name, no member — `app` has no `ITEM_KEY_DISCRIMINATORS` entry). The body-as-app document is the whole body (`registerAppNotingStamp` registers the manifest itself), which is what an `app` override of a legacy one-app package replaces whole, so comparing the body is the right document; `version` is dropped because it names the release and would differ on every upgrade, and the `_`-stamps are already stripped by `itemText`. The two new pins cover `apps[]` changed/unchanged and body-as-app changed/version-bump-only. The header now also states the `translation` boundary (no item seam) that the first record asked for. The gap is closed; one spelling of the condition, read from the engine, as the seat ordered.

**Is `engine-registration.ts` behaviour-identical? Yes.** Two sites changed, both from the literal `Boolean(manifest.name && manifest.navigation && !manifest.apps?.length)` to `registersManifestAsApp(manifest)`, whose body is `Boolean(manifest?.name && manifest?.navigation && !manifest?.apps?.length)`. The only textual difference is optional chaining on `manifest`, and at both sites `manifest` is the object `convertPackageBodyForward(registeredBody)` returned and already dereferenced (`manifest.id || manifest.name`, line 100) before either site runs, so `manifest?.` and `manifest.` evaluate identically there. The nested-plugin site (line 123, `Boolean(plugin.name && plugin.navigation)`, no `apps` term) is a different condition and was correctly left alone — it is step 7's, not step 4's. No registration order, stamp or log line moved.

**Do the merged-in changes interact with the advisory code? No.** Against the branch parent the merge changes nothing under `packages/objectql`, `packages/metadata-core`, `packages/core`, `packages/spec/src/{kernel,ui,meta-spelling}`, `packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts` or `packages/cli/src/commands/package`. Under `packages/metadata-protocol` it brings `protocol.ts` (one hunk at line 11154 in an unrelated method, and import lines), `protocol-package-install.ts`, `protocol-package-commits.ts`; under `packages/cloud-connection` the unmanaged-copy region of the install door and its tests (#31570) — none of them the dry run, the schema gate, `convertPackageBodyForward`, `listServedOverrides` or `isServedOverrideRowOf`. The merge against `main` is byte-for-byte the PR's own fifteen files. The regenerated reference page is downstream of a `.describe()` that moved on `main`, not of this PR's text.

**Nits (no effect on correctness or the contract):**
- `engine-top-level.ts`: `registersManifestAsApp` was inserted between the existing JSDoc of `packageBodyObjectAndAppOwnerStampRefusal` (the block ending `@param scope …`) and that function, so two docblocks now sit back to back and the older one is attached to nothing while the new one documents the predicate.
